question: I'm a full-time federal employee with 2 years of service. How much annual leave do I earn each pay period?
answer: A full-time federal employee with less than 3 years of service earns one-half day of annual leave for each full biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)].
gold_answer: 4 hours (½ day) per biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(1)]

question: I've worked full-time for the government for 4 years. How many hours of annual leave do I get per pay period?
answer: For full-time employees with 3 but less than 15 years of service, annual leave accrues at ¾ day (6 hours) for each full biweekly pay period, except for the last pay period in the year, which accrues 1¼ day (10 hours) [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)]. Therefore, you accrue 6 hours of annual leave per pay period.
gold_answer: 6 hours (¾ day) per pay period; 10 hours in the last full pay period of the year [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)]

question: How much annual leave per pay period does a full-time employee with 16 years of service earn?
answer: A full-time employee with 16 years of service earns 1 day of annual leave for each full biweekly pay period. [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(3)(ii)(B)]
gold_answer: 8 hours (1 day) per pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(3)]

question: How many hours of annual leave does a full-time employee with 4 years of service earn in a whole year?
answer: A full-time employee with 4 years of service earns 6 hours of annual leave for each pay period, except for the last pay period in the year, which accrues 10 hours. [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Entitlement]

question: What is the maximum amount of annual leave most federal employees can carry over into the next leave year?
answer: The maximum amount of annual leave most federal employees can carry over into the next leave year is 30 days [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings].
gold_answer: 240 hours (30 days) [5 U.S.C. 6304(a)]

question: How much annual leave can a federal employee stationed overseas carry over?
answer: A federal employee stationed overseas may carry over up to 45 days of annual leave into the new leave year, as specified in the OPM fact sheet [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings]. This applies to employees who meet the requirements outlined in 5 U.S.C. 6304(b).
gold_answer: 45 days (360 hours) [5 U.S.C. 6304(b)]

question: What is the annual leave carryover limit for Senior Executive Service members?
answer: The annual leave carryover limit for Senior Executive Service members is 90 days (720 hours) [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings]. This ceiling applies to members of the Senior Executive Service, Senior-Level, and Scientific and Professional Employees as determined by OPM [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings].
gold_answer: 90 days (720 hours) [5 U.S.C. 6304(f)]

question: How fast does a full-time federal employee accrue sick leave?
answer: A full-time federal employee accrues sick leave at a rate of one-half day for each full biweekly pay period, except for members of the Firefighting Division of the Fire Department of the District of Columbia, who accrue two-fifths of a day for each full biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6307(a) to 6307(d)].
gold_answer: 4 hours (½ day) per biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6307(a)]

question: Is there a cap on how much sick leave I can accumulate?
answer: There is no general cap on the amount of sick leave that can be accumulated [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information) > Sick Leave Accumulation]. However, for part-time employees or those on an uncommon tour of duty, the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) may establish proportional limitations [5 U.S.C. 6307(d)(3)(i) to 6307(d)(4)(B)]. Additionally, a full-time employee may not accumulate more than 240 hours (30 days) of advanced sick leave at any one time [OPM fact sheet: Advanced Sick Leave > Maximum Amount of Advanced Sick Leave].
gold_answer: No, there is no limit on accumulated sick leave [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information)]

question: How many hours of sick leave can I use in a leave year for general family care or bereavement?
answer: An employee is entitled to use up to 104 hours (13 days) of sick leave each leave year for general family care or bereavement purposes [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information) > Sick Leave Usage Limits per Leave Year].
gold_answer: Up to 104 hours (13 days) per leave year [5 CFR 630.401(b)]

question: How much sick leave can I use to care for a family member with a serious health condition?
answer: You are entitled to use up to 12 weeks (480 hours) of sick leave each leave year to care for a family member with a serious health condition [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave to Care for a Family Member with a Serious Health Condition > Sick Leave Entitlement].
gold_answer: Up to 480 hours (12 administrative workweeks) per leave year [5 CFR 630.401(c)]

question: How much FMLA leave is a federal employee entitled to?
answer: A covered Federal employee is entitled to a total of 12 workweeks of unpaid FMLA leave during any 12-month period for qualifying reasons, including qualifying exigencies related to a spouse, son, daughter, or parent on covered active duty in the Armed Forces [5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1)].
gold_answer: 12 administrative workweeks in any 12-month period [5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1)]

question: How much paid parental leave can a federal employee take after the birth of a child?
answer: A federal employee can take up to 12 administrative workweeks of Paid Parental Leave (PPL) following the birth of a child, as provided by the Federal Employee Paid Leave Act [5 U.S.C. 6382]. This leave may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave. The PPL entitlement is available for qualifying births or placements occurring on or after October 1, 2020. The PPL must be used within a 12-month period following the birth or placement. [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Introduction]
gold_answer: 12 administrative workweeks of paid parental leave [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]

question: How many days of leave can I get to donate bone marrow?
answer: An employee may use up to 7 days of paid leave each calendar year to serve as a bone-marrow donor [5 U.S.C. 6327(a) to 6327(c)]. This leave is in addition to annual and sick leave [OPM fact sheet: Bone Marrow or Organ Donor Leave]. The Office of Personnel Management may prescribe regulations for the administration of this section [5 U.S.C. 6327].
gold_answer: Up to 7 days [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(1)]

question: How much leave is available to a federal employee who donates an organ?
answer: A federal employee who donates an organ is entitled to up to 30 days of paid leave each calendar year for that purpose. This leave is in addition to annual and sick leave. The entitlement is specified in 5 U.S.C. 6327(a) to 6327(c).
gold_answer: Up to 30 days [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(2)]

question: What is the maximum disabled veteran leave a new employee can be credited?
answer: The maximum disabled veteran leave a new employee can be credited is 104 hours, provided they are under a regular full-time work schedule. For part-time or seasonal schedules, the credit is proportionally equivalent based on the hours in the work schedule [OPM fact sheet: Disabled Veteran Leave > Crediting of Hours by Work Schedule]. This credit is subject to offset by the employee's existing sick leave balance as of the first day of employment [5 CFR 630.1305(d)].
gold_answer: Up to 104 hours [5 U.S.C. 6329(b)(1)]

question: What is the most sick leave an agency can advance to an employee?
answer: The most sick leave an agency can advance to a full-time employee is 240 hours (30 days) [5 CFR 630.402(b)]. For part-time employees, the amount is prorated based on their regularly scheduled workweek [5 CFR 630.402].
gold_answer: Up to 240 hours (30 days) [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information)]

question: Under the Emergency Leave Transfer Program, how much donated annual leave can one recipient receive at a time?
answer: Under the Emergency Leave Transfer Program, an emergency leave recipient may receive a maximum of 240 hours of donated annual leave at any one time for each disaster or emergency [5 CFR 630.1111]. Additionally, an employing agency may allow additional disbursements of donated annual leave based on the employee's continuing need, with each disbursement not exceeding 240 hours.
gold_answer: Up to 240 hours per disaster or emergency at any one time [OPM fact sheet: Emergency Leave Transfer Program]

question: If I scheduled annual leave in advance but got sick and couldn't use it before the year ended, can it be restored?
answer: If you scheduled annual leave in advance but got sick and couldn't use it before the year ended, it may be restored only under very limited conditions. Specifically, annual leave forfeited due to sickness can be restored if it was scheduled in writing before the start of the third biweekly pay period prior to the end of the leave year [OPM fact sheet: Importance of Scheduling "Use or Lose" Leave in Advance]. If not scheduled in advance, restoration is generally not allowed unless under exceptional circumstances such as national emergencies or administrative error [OPM fact sheet: Importance of Scheduling "Use or Lose" Leave in Advance]. Contact your agency HR office for specific guidance.
gold_answer: Yes, annual leave lost because of sickness when scheduled in advance is restored [5 U.S.C. 6304(d)(1)(C)]

answer: The provided policy documents do not cover this.
gold_answer: $116,071 [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, DCB]

question: What is the overtime hourly rate for a GS-12 step 5 in the Washington DC area in 2026?
answer: The overtime hourly rate for a GS-12 step 5 in the Washington DC area in 2026 is calculated as the employee's hourly rate of basic pay multiplied by 1.5, as per [OPM fact sheet: Overtime Pay Title 5 > Overtime Hourly Rate]. The hourly rate of basic pay would be determined by dividing the annual rate of basic pay by 2,087 hours. The annual rate of basic pay for a GS-12 step 5 in Washington DC in 2026 is $96,886, as per [OPM fact sheet: Simultaneous Pay Actions > Geographic Conversion Rule]. Thus, the hourly rate is $96,886 / 2,087 ≈ $46.41, and the overtime hourly rate is $46.41 × 1.5 = $69.62.
gold_answer: $55.89 per hour [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, DCB]

question: What does a GS-9 step 1 earn per year in the Rest of U.S. locality in 2026?
answer: The GS-9 step 1 locality rate in the Rest of U.S. (RUS) locality for 2026 is $72,303. This is calculated as the 2025 RUS locality rate multiplied by the 2026 locality rate factor of 1.1706, resulting in $72,303. [OPM fact sheet: January 2026 Pay Examples > 2. GS employee promoted on same day the 2026 pay adjustments take effect (standard method)].
gold_answer: $61,722 per year; $29.57/hour [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, RUS]

question: Which federal holidays fall in December 2026?
answer: [OPM fact sheet: Holidays Work Schedules and Pay > Holidays for Federal Employees] The federal holiday in December 2026 is Christmas Day on December 25.
gold_answer: Christmas Day, Friday 25 December 2026

question: What date is Thanksgiving in 2026 for federal employees?
answer: Thanksgiving Day for federal employees in 2026 is on the fourth Thursday in November, which is November 25, 2026. [OPM fact sheet: Holidays Work Schedules and Pay > Holidays for Federal Employees]
gold_answer: Thursday 26 November 2026

question: I'm part-time with 5 years of service and had 52 hours in a pay status this pay period. How much annual and sick leave did I earn?
answer: A part-time employee with 5 years of service earns 1 hour of annual leave for each 13 hours in a pay status. For 52 hours in a pay status, you earned 4 hours of annual leave. The provided policy documents do not cover sick leave accrual specifically. Contact your agency HR office for details on sick leave. [5 CFR 630.303]
gold_answer: 4 hours annual (52/13) and 2.6 hours sick (52/20) [5 U.S.C. 6303(a); 6307(a)]

answer: The provided policy documents do not cover this.
gold_answer: 10 hours would be forfeited (250 − 240 cap) [5 U.S.C. 6304(a)]

question: Do I get extra pay for regularly scheduled night work, and how much?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to extra pay for regularly scheduled night work. The extra pay, known as night pay, is a 10 percent differential of your rate of basic pay, including any applicable locality payment or special rate supplement [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)]. This applies to work performed between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m. [5 CFR 550.121(a)].
gold_answer: Yes, a night differential of 10% of basic pay for regularly scheduled work between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m. [5 CFR 550.121(a)]

question: What premium pay do I get for working on a Sunday as part of my regular schedule?
answer: You are entitled to Sunday premium pay equal to 25 percent of your rate of basic pay for each hour of Sunday work. Sunday work consists of nonovertime work during your regularly scheduled basic tour of duty (not to exceed 8 hours) that begins or ends on a Sunday. If you are on a compressed work schedule, all nonovertime hours in your regularly scheduled daily tour of duty beginning or ending on a Sunday constitutes Sunday work. [OPM fact sheet: Sunday Premium Pay > Entitlement] [OPM fact sheet: Sunday Premium Pay > Compressed Work Schedule]
gold_answer: Basic pay plus 25% premium pay for each hour of Sunday work [5 CFR 550.171(a)]

question: For a non-exempt employee, at what rate is overtime paid under the FLSA and when does it start?
answer: Overtime pay for nonexempt employees is calculated at one and one-half times the employee's hourly regular rate of pay, starting after 8 hours in a day or 40 hours in a workweek [5 U.S.C. 6121]. The hourly regular rate is determined by dividing the total remuneration paid in the workweek by the number of hours worked [5 CFR 551.501(a)(6)].
gold_answer: 1.5 times the regular rate for hours over 8 in a day or 40 in a workweek [5 CFR 551.501(a)]

question: How many hours is the basic workweek for a full-time federal employee?
answer: The basic workweek for a full-time federal employee is 40 hours, as specified in [5 CFR 610.111(a)(1)].
gold_answer: 40 hours, not over more than 6 of any 7 consecutive days [5 CFR 610.111(a)(1)]

question: How long do I need to have worked for the government before I can use FMLA leave?
answer: To be eligible for FMLA leave, you must have at least 12 months of qualifying civilian or military service. This service does not need to be consecutive or recent and can include service at one or more agencies. Qualifying civilian service includes employment as defined in 5 U.S.C. 2105, such as with the U.S. Postal Service or non-appropriated fund instrumentality. Military service must be honorable active service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps. [OPM fact sheet: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) 12-Week Entitlement > 12 Months of Qualifying Civilian or Military Service]
gold_answer: At least 12 months of service [5 U.S.C. 6381(1)(B)]

question: Can I take compensatory time off instead of being paid for irregular overtime?
answer: Yes, you may take compensatory time off instead of being paid for irregular or occasional overtime work, provided it is approved by your agency head or designee [5 CFR 550.114(a) to 550.114(b)]. This applies to both FLSA exempt and nonexempt employees who are covered by the definition of "employee" at 5 U.S.C. 5541(2) [OPM fact sheet: Compensatory Time Off > Employee Coverage].
gold_answer: Yes, at the employee's request the agency may grant compensatory time off instead of overtime pay [5 CFR 550.114(a)]

question: What is the maximum recruitment incentive as a share of annual basic pay?
answer: The maximum recruitment incentive as a share of annual basic pay is 25 percent, unless a waiver is granted. With a waiver, it may increase to 50 percent. [5 CFR 575.109(b)(1)] and [5 CFR 575.109(c)(1)].
gold_answer: Generally up to 25% of annual basic pay for the service period [5 CFR 575.109(b)(1)]

question: What is the maximum retention incentive an individual employee can be authorized?
answer: The maximum retention incentive an individual employee can be authorized is 25 percent of the employee's basic pay, unless a waiver is granted. A waiver allows up to 50 percent if the employee's qualifications are critical to an important agency mission, project, or initiative [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)].
gold_answer: 25% of basic pay for an individual employee [5 CFR 575.309(a)(1)]

question: I'm at GS step 2. How long must I wait for my next within-grade increase?
answer: [OPM fact sheet: Quality Step Increase > Timing Matters] [5 CFR 531.405(a)] If you are at GS step 2, you must complete 52 calendar weeks of creditable service to be eligible for your next within-grade increase. This waiting period begins on your first appointment as a Federal employee or on receiving an equivalent increase.
gold_answer: 52 calendar weeks of creditable service (steps 1–3) [5 CFR 531.405(a)]

question: How long is the waiting period between step 5 and step 6?
answer: The waiting period between step 5 and step 6 is 104 weeks of creditable service in step 5 [OPM fact sheet: Within-Grade Increases > Required Waiting Periods].
gold_answer: 104 calendar weeks (steps 4–6) [5 CFR 531.405(a)]

question: How long is the wait for a within-grade increase once I'm at step 7 or above?
answer: The waiting period for a within-grade increase once you are at step 7 or above is 156 calendar weeks. This applies to employees without a scheduled tour of duty, as stated in [5 CFR 531.405(a)(2)(iii) to 531.405(b)(2)].
gold_answer: 156 calendar weeks [5 CFR 531.405(a)(iii)]

question: What is the most administrative leave an agency can place an employee on in a calendar year?
answer: The most administrative leave an agency can place an employee on in a calendar year is 10 workdays, as specified in 5 U.S.C. 6329a(b)(1) and 5 CFR 630.1404(a). This limit applies specifically to administrative leave for investigative purposes. [5 U.S.C. 6329a(b)(1)] [5 CFR 630.1404(a)]
gold_answer: No more than 10 work days per calendar year [5 U.S.C. 6329a(b)(1)]

question: When does the federal leave year begin?
answer: The federal leave year begins on the first day of the first full biweekly pay period in a calendar year [OPM fact sheet: Leave Year Beginning and Ending Dates > Fact Sheet: Leave Year Beginning and Ending Dates].
gold_answer: On the first day of the first full biweekly pay period in the calendar year [OPM fact sheet: Leave Year]

question: If my office closes for a snowstorm, can my agency give me paid leave?
answer: If your office closes due to a snowstorm, your agency may provide you with paid weather and safety leave under 5 U.S.C. 6329c, provided you are prevented from safely traveling to or performing work at an approved location. [5 U.S.C. 6329c(b)(1) to 6329c(d)(2)]. However, this leave cannot be given if you are on other preapproved leave or if you are using it to replace a regular day off. [5 CFR 630.1606(c)]. Agencies must record this leave separately. [5 U.S.C. 6329c(d)(2)].
gold_answer: Yes, weather and safety leave without loss of pay may be approved [5 U.S.C. 6329c(b)]

question: Do I have to agree to keep working for my agency after taking paid parental leave?
answer: Yes, you are required to agree to keep working for your agency after taking paid parental leave. [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Advanced Written Service Agreement] Prior to using paid parental leave (PPL), you must enter into a written service agreement to work for the applicable employing agency for not less than 12 weeks after the day on which PPL concludes. This 12-week work obligation is statutorily fixed and applies regardless of the actual amount of leave used. If you fail to return for the required 12 weeks of work, the agency may require reimbursement for Government contributions made to maintain your health insurance coverage during the period of paid parental leave.
gold_answer: Yes, you must agree in writing beforehand to work for the agency for at least 12 weeks after the leave ends [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]

question: Is there a minimum length of service to be eligible for paid parental leave?
answer: Yes, an employee must have at least 12 months of qualifying Federal service to be eligible for paid parental leave (PPL), as PPL is a type of paid leave substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, and eligibility for FMLA leave requires 12 months of qualifying service [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Key Features of PPL]. Employees with temporary appointments, intermittent work schedules, or fewer than 12 months of qualifying service are not eligible for FMLA leave and thus not eligible for PPL.
gold_answer: Yes, at least 12 months of service before the birth or placement [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]

question: I'm GS-12 step 5 in the Washington DC area. How much overtime pay do I earn for 2 hours of overtime in 2026?
answer: To calculate your FLSA overtime pay for 2 hours of overtime in 2026, first determine your hourly rate of basic pay. For a GS-12, step 5, employee in the Washington, DC, locality pay area in 2026, your annual rate of basic pay is $101,400 (based on the 2026 salary table). Divide this by 2,087 hours to get your hourly rate: $101,400 / 2,087 ≈ $48.60. Your overtime hourly rate is $48.60 × 1.5 = $72.90. For 2 hours of overtime, you would earn 2 × $72.90 = $145.80. [5 U.S.C. 5542(a)(2)]
gold_answer: 2 × $55.89 = $111.78 [OPM 2026 GS pay table (DCB)]
